steps.say: Ischaemic priapism is a closed box emergency of the penis. The low flow erection is painful and rock hard, with no arterial blood entering and acid and oxygen lack building inside. Trapped unoxygenated blood turns the shafts into a sealed compartment, and every hour without drainage kills more tissue.
steps.tx: **Ischemic priapism** (**low-flow priapism**, veno-occlusive compartment emergency) is a painful rigid erection with no arterial inflow to the corpora and worsening cavernosal acid and oxygen lack. Imprisoned deoxygenated blood makes the corpora a closed **compartment emergency** (tissue dying in a sealed space), and elapsed time directly predicts smooth muscle death.

vis.caption: Cavernosal anatomy behind the low-flow compartment emergency. Credit: BruceBlaus, CC BY-SA, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Blood gas identifies the type at the bedside. Ischaemic blood shows deep acid and oxygen lack with pH under seven point two five, oxygen under thirty, and waste gas over sixty. High flow samples read arterial instead, so the gas alone tells emergency apart from non emergency.
steps.tx: **Cavernosal blood gas** (needle sampling of corporal blood) in ischemia reads like venous blood left too long: **pH <7.25** (acid), **pO2 <30 mmHg** (no oxygen), and **pCO2 >60 mmHg** (high). Non-ischemic high-flow gases read arterial instead, so the reading alone distinguishes emergency from non-emergency at the bedside.

steps.say: High flow priapism is a different disease. The arterial form is usually painless and soft, caused by a straddle injury that tears a small artery and opens a direct leak into the erectile sponge. Oxygen rich blood flows straight through without trapping, so there is no acid, no pain, and no urgency.
steps.tx: **Non-ischemic priapism** (**arterial priapism**, high-flow leak) is typically painless and non-rigid, caused by blunt perineal trauma tearing an arteriole into an uncontrolled cavernosal **arteriolar fistula** (arteriolar-sinusoidal short circuit). Oxygenated blood transits without trapping, so no acidosis, pain, or urgency develops, only a prolonged semi-erection needing no emergency drainage.

rows: None: no acidosis, no tissue death

steps.say: First treatment is washout plus vessel tightening drugs. The shafts are drained and flushed with salt water to remove acid blood, then phenylephrine is injected inside at one hundred to five hundred micrograms per millilitre every three to five minutes. Blood pressure and pulse are watched throughout because absorbed drug can spike pressure.
steps.tx: First therapy is **corporal aspiration** (needle drainage) with saline irrigation to remove acidotic blood, then intracavernosal **phenylephrine** (**alpha-1 agonist**, vasoconstrictor) **100 to 500 mcg/mL** (one hundred to five hundred micrograms per millilitre) **every 3 to 5 minutes** (three to five). Pressure and pulse are monitored throughout because systemic absorption can spike blood pressure, especially in older men.

vis.alt: Sagittal penile diagram showing phimosis, paraphimosis, and urethral lesions on examination.
vis.caption: Penile examination mapping ischaemic rigidity before aspiration. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: When drugs fail, drainage goes through the tip. Needle shunts named Winter and Ebbehoj drive a wide needle or blade from the tip into the shafts, opening a channel between tip and shaft. Blood escapes through the new window, the erection falls, and the puncture heals with little harm.
steps.tx: Percutaneous **distal shunt** (glans-to-corpora needle channel) procedures, the **Winter shunt** and **Ebbehoj shunt** (large-bore needle or scalpel shunts), open a channel from glans penis into the corpora cavernosa. Blood leaves through the new window, the erection subsides, and the puncture heals with little harm.

steps.say: Open tip shunts remove a core of wall. The Al-Ghorab and Burnett operations cut a five millimetre disc of tough sheath through the tip, making a larger lasting window for outflow. Their indication is needle shunt failure, accepting a bigger tip wound for dependable drainage.
steps.tx: Open distal shunts, the **Al-Ghorab shunt** and **Burnett shunt** (excisional glans windows), remove a **5 mm** (five millimetre) disc or oval of distal tunica albuginea through the glans to restore outflow. Needle shunt failure is their indication, accepting a bigger glans wound for dependable drainage.

rows: 5 mm circle or ellipse of distal tunica

steps.say: Base shunts drain blood at the root. The Quackels join links shaft to sponge at the perineum, while the Grayhack join links leg vein to shaft. Both move blood from rigid shafts into low pressure systems, and both are kept for cases where tip shunting cannot be done or has failed.
steps.tx: **Proximal shunt** (base-level rerouting) options are the **Quackels shunt** (corporospongiosal anastomosis at the perineum) and the **Grayhack shunt** (saphenous vein-to-corpus cavernosum anastomosis). Both drain rigid corpora into low-pressure systems, and both are reserved for cases where distal shunting is impossible or has failed.

rows: Drain rigid corpora to low pressure

steps.say: Delay scars the erectile tissue beyond rescue. Ischaemia past thirty six to forty eight hours kills all smooth muscle and leaves a scarred useless penis. Putting a prosthesis in at once ends the priapism and holds length, preventing the shortening that scarring would otherwise impose.
steps.tx: Ischemia beyond **36 to 48 hours** (thirty six to forty eight) causes complete cavernosal **smooth muscle necrosis** (muscle death) and fibrosis, leaving a scarred non-functional penis. **Immediate prosthesis** (early penile implant) insertion resolves the priapism and preserves length, preventing the shortening that fibrosis would otherwise impose.

rows: Complete smooth muscle necrosis then fibrosis
